metadata.name: unzip
metadata.displayName: unzip - Extract files from ZIP archives

installation.note: unzip is typically pre-installed on Ubuntu, but can be installed with: sudo apt install unzip

overview.summary: The unzip command extracts files from ZIP archives. ZIP is a widely used archive format, especially common on Windows systems and for distributing software. unzip can extract entire archives or specific files, list archive contents, and handle password-protected archives.
when_to_use: Extract ZIP archives downloaded from the internet
Extract files from Windows-created ZIP files
Extract specific files from large archives

syntax.description: Extract files from ZIPFILE. If FILE arguments are provided, only those files are extracted. Use -x to exclude files.

options.use_case: See what's in a ZIP file before extracting
Extract to a specific location instead of current directory
Automatically overwrite existing files in scripts

options.description: Use password to decrypt encrypted ZIP files
options.use_case: Extract password-protected ZIP files (less secure - password visible in command history)
Extract archive but skip certain files or patterns

misconceptions.title: unzip extracts to archive's original location
misconceptions.misconception: unzip extracts files to where they were originally located
misconceptions.reality: unzip extracts files to the current directory (or -d specified directory). The original location doesn't matter.
misconceptions.tip: Use -d to specify extraction location: unzip -d /path/to/extract archive.zip

misconceptions.title: unzip can extract any archive format
misconceptions.misconception: unzip works with all archive formats (tar, gzip, etc.)
misconceptions.reality: unzip only works with ZIP format (.zip files). Use tar for .tar, .tar.gz, .tar.bz2, gunzip for .gz, etc.
misconceptions.tip: Each archive format has its own tool: unzip for .zip, tar for .tar, gunzip for .gz

common_pitfalls.description: unzip may prompt to overwrite existing files, which can interrupt scripts
common_pitfalls.solution: Use -o to overwrite automatically, or -n to never overwrite, in scripts

common_pitfalls.description: Files extract to current directory, which might not be intended
common_pitfalls.solution: Always use -d to specify destination, or cd to desired directory first

common_pitfalls.description: Using -P password exposes password in shell history
common_pitfalls.solution: For password-protected files, let unzip prompt interactively, or use environment variables

related_commands.relationship: Archive creation; zip creates ZIP files, unzip extracts them
Alternative extraction; gunzip handles .gz files, unzip handles .zip files

best_practices: Use -l to list contents before extracting large archives
Always use -d to specify extraction directory in scripts
Use -o in scripts to avoid prompts, or -n to prevent overwrites
Use -q for silent extraction in automated processes
Check archive contents first with -l to avoid extracting unwanted files
performance_tips: Extracting specific files is faster than extracting entire archives
Use -q for faster extraction when you don't need progress output
Large archives extract faster to local disks than network mounts

additional_notes.format_support: unzip supports standard ZIP format and some ZIP64 extensions for large files
additional_notes.password_protection: Supports password-protected ZIP files, but -P flag is insecure (visible in history)
additional_notes.directory_structure: Preserves directory structure from archive when extracting
additional_notes.windows_compatibility: Works well with ZIP files created on Windows systems
